subject: [RFC PATCH 03/57] mm/collapse: add collapse.h for the shared collapse state

2026-08-16.patch_summary: This patch adds a new header file mm/collapse.h to store shared state between the collapse engine and khugepaged.c. It includes an enum scan_result and struct collapse_control, which define various states and control structures for page scanning and allocation. The patch moves these definitions from khugepaged.c to the new header file, with no functional changes intended. This is a preparatory step for building the new collapse engine in its own file.

reviews.author: Lorenzo (ARM)
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that introducing a new file requires updating MAINTAINERS, specifically the THP section, and requested this change be included in the same patch.
reviews.raw_body:
Any change that introduces a new file should in the same change update
MAINTAINERS (in the THP section to which this belongs :)

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledges reviewer's concern about the patch causing significant churn and potential issues with blame tracking, offers to restructure in v2 if preferred.
reviews.raw_body:
I went for a clean collapse.c on purpose: the engine is new code, and a
new file keeps it readable while both mechanisms are in the tree, with 28
as a plain delete from khugepaged.c.

Your shape is less churn, though, and it keeps blame: 29-35 move about
1700 lines as add-and-delete today, and most of that would stay put, with
only the daemon -- mm_slot, the scan loop, sysfs -- extracted into a new
khugepaged.c.

If you prefer it that way, I can give it a try for v2.

The rename has to open the series, so it will collide with anything in
flight that touches khugepaged.c.

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer David (Arm) expressed concern that the patch's writing style is inconsistent with the author's usual tone, citing specific examples of unnatural phrasing and suggesting that the LLM should preserve the original tone and focus on grammar corrections.
reviews.raw_body:
It doesn't read the way you would usually write. In a bad way.

E.g., "Your shape", "has to open the series"

Consider telling the LLM to not change your writing style and focus only on
fixing grammar.

Otherwise it will be very load bearing to read and we'll be sorry to have to
gently push back against that.


Imagine I would instead have written the following:

The text does not read the way you would normally write, and the difference is
noticeable in a way that makes it feel less natural.

For example, phrases such as \u201cYour shape\u201d and \u201chas to open the series\u201d do not
sound consistent with your usual writing style.

It may be worth instructing the LLM to preserve your original tone and phrasing
as much as possible, and to focus only on correcting grammar and obvious
language issues.

-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: Lorenzo (ARM)
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Lorenzo requested the patch be broken down into a smaller initial series, citing his own experience with a scalable CoW series as an example, and suggested that this would lay better foundations for future development.

The reviewer expressed frustration with the large number of changes in the patch, suggesting that the author generate human-written responses instead of relying on AI-generated ones.
reviews.raw_body:
Please don't respin this as a 57 patch series.

You need to break this into a smaller initial series that lays some
foundations.

Cf. what I've done with scalable CoW series as an example.

---

Even this reads as AI-generated... Consider writing the replies yourself
please.

You've generated a ton of work here and the AI-style giant replies just
create more.

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledges that the patch series is too large and promises to split it into smaller, self-contained patches for review.
reviews.raw_body:
I didn't plan to.

The goal of this RFC was to show the final form I want to reach.

I will move cleanups and refactoring to the front of the patchset and
submit in small self-contained chunks while keeping the rest working in
a private branch.

reviews.author: Lorenzo (ARM)
reviews.summary: Reviewer Lorenzo expressed concerns that the patch series is overwhelming due to its large size, and suggested that writing summaries of LLMs (Large Language Models) in replies would help alleviate this issue.
reviews.raw_body:
Sorry that wasn't intended as personal. Text is a bad medium.

What I meant to say is I agree with David re: the use of LLMs in replies, it's
not helpful in that it leads to the usual issue of very large blocks of texts
that are difficult to parse.

So put in a clearer way - I meant to say that writing them yourself would avoid
this issue.

My experience is that the series as a whole is overwhelming to review in its
current form, and adding more material to get through this way makes it more
difficult.

Hopefully this clears up what I was trying to say... :)
